title: Dressing
description: What the *map* looks like where the sim has only a tile class. A Low tile is 'cover you can shoot over' to every mechanism that walks, sees or shoots -- the sim knows nothing finer -- and this entry is what says a run of them is a wrecked car and a lone one is a dumpster. Same rule as prop.schema.json and for the same reason (CLAUDE.md, 'how a thing looks is content, not code'): presentation/dressing.gd resolves keys out of this block and main.gd blits them, and neither contains a sprite key of its own. NOTE: the content validator is shallow -- it checks these top-level types and rejects unexpected top-level keys, and never once looks inside `wrecks` -- so the whole nested shape below is enforced by check_wrecks.gd, which resolves every key it declares and refuses a fabricated one.

id.description: Stable namespaced id. presentation/dressing.gd names exactly one, BLOCK_ID.

name.description: Human-readable name. Never shown to the player -- the district describes itself in prose, not in labels.

wrecks.description: How a Low tile draws. `variants` is a list of {id, front, mid, rear} car segment sets, each authored north-facing over one tile; a run of two takes front+rear and a run of three front+mid+rear, and the variant for a whole run is picked by a pure hash of the map seed and the run's anchor tile (never a sim RNG stream -- presentation may not spend a draw the layout would have to account for). An east-west run draws the same north-authored keys through a quarter-turn transform, which is why there is no second set of keys for it. An optional `solo` key draws a Low tile that has no Low neighbour, which is one tile long and therefore not a car; none is declared today (see docs/23 -- the skip was drawn and cut with the worldgen change that would have stood more of them), and a lone Low tile draws the renderer's procedural cover block instead.

litter.description: Cosmetic scatter keys for street pavement, hash-picked per tile and sparse. Purely decorative: litter marks nothing, blocks nothing and is drawn on tiles the sim considers empty paving.

rubble.description: Scatter keys drawn over tiles whose surface layer is SURFACE_RUBBLE -- the ground the worldgen rubble pass places. Unlike litter this one lies over something the sim does read (rubble slows a body and loudens a step), but the art still says nothing the surface did not already say.

walls.description: Wall material name -> {cap, face} sprite keys, one entry per building.schema.json / map.schema.json `look.wall` value. Optional, and the shallow validator never looks inside it -- it checks only that `walls` itself is an object -- so check_roof_look.gd is what resolves every key a shipped template's `look.wall` names and refuses one with no entry here.

roofs.description: Roof material name -> sprite keys, one entry per building.schema.json / map.schema.json `look.roof` value: `{n, s}` for a pitched material (north/south faces) or `{flat}` for a flat one. Optional, and the shallow validator never looks inside it -- it checks only that `roofs` itself is an object -- so check_roof_look.gd is what resolves every key a shipped template's `look.roof` names and refuses one with no entry here.

faces.description: Fixed sprite keys for the wall openings a building shell cuts, independent of wall material: `{window, door, garage}`. Optional, and the shallow validator never looks inside it -- it checks only that `faces` itself is an object -- so check_roof_look.gd is what resolves every key it declares and refuses a fabricated one.

trees.description: How a Tree tile draws: `tall` is a list of sprite keys, each a 32x96 feet-anchored picture (Appearance.TREE_CANVAS) that presentation/main.gd stands on the trunk tile's south-edge centre and y-sorts with the bodies, picked per tile by a pure hash of the seed and the tile (Dressing.SALT_TREE). Optional: a block with no trees draws the two procedural discs the tile branch always drew. The shallow validator never looks inside; check_trees.gd resolves every key at its canvas and refuses a fabricated one.
